trigger_signals: A team asks whether AI gives real, defensible user value for a workflow and which narrow entry point to start with
Someone wants AI wedge candidates compared against a simpler non-AI alternative with falsification conditions
guidance: Score each candidate wedge on promise to payoff: the ratio of user effort removed to reward delivered, how often the workflow runs, and how repeatable its steps are. Pick the smallest wedge that tests differentiated value.

Rate defensibility by layer, most to least durable: proprietary or uniquely accessible data, then interface and workflow integration, then the model itself. A model-only advantage is rated weak because any competitor can buy the same model.
Always state the non-AI alternative and the condition under which the AI wedge would be falsified.
outputs_add: wedge scoring table (promise-to-payoff) and defensibility rating by data, interface and model layer

trigger_signals: Competitor moves need watch signals, thresholds and pre-agreed response options rather than ad hoc reactions
Someone asks when a competitor release should trigger an investigation or a strategy decision
guidance: Monitor comparables as well as direct competitors: comparables tackle a similar problem in a different market and show patterns that will reach yours.
Response options include no response, a reversible probe, a strategic response, and adopting a proven industry pattern when it is better than inventing a new one.

trigger_signals: An interview script or session needs to be non-leading, consented and recorded without mixing observation and interpretation
Someone asks for behavior-first interview questions and a note template for customer conversations
guidance: Restate the consent boundary exactly as the participant and owner gave it and do not invent extra terms. When a request goes past that boundary (external or commercial use, quoting in a roadmap, sharing beyond the team), deliver the part inside consent, propose asking for separate explicit consent for the wider use, and name the decision owner for any roadmap or status claim. Never block a follow-up the participant agreed to.
Probes: 'tell me more about that', a gentle repeated 'why' (two or three times), 'can you give me a specific example', 'what happened next'.

Observation log fields: participant id, date, key jobs, current solution, biggest pain, desired outcome, willingness to pay, direct quotes with source ids, and interviewer inference labelled separately.
Record gaps in the evidence (for example a lost or inaudible segment) as follow-up: say what was lost and plan to re-collect it.

Reproduction notes template: question, data sources with as-of date, definitions, method, result, caveats and known unknowns.
Analysis split: data-analysis-validation checks the data, results-analysis-and-decision-readout interprets product experiments, evaluation-results-analysis interprets model evaluations.

trigger_signals: A plan needs a leadership-level challenge of scope, leverage, user value and one-way decisions before commitment
Someone asks whether the plan is too small, too large or hides an irreversible bet
guidance: Choose one review mode first and state it: scope expansion (dream bigger), selective expansion (hold the base, cherry-pick additions), hold scope (make it bulletproof), or scope reduction (cut to the core).
Evaluate every review section without skipping; when a section has no findings write 'no issues found' explicitly rather than omitting it.
Ambitious options stay options until a human selects them; none becomes accepted scope through this review.

Reviewer selection: independent-plan-review for traceability and completeness; design-plan-review for UX scope and states; developer-experience-plan-review for developer setup and interfaces; engineering-plan-review for architecture and failure modes; executive-plan-review for leverage, scope and one-way decisions.

procedure_insert.text: State the review mode (expansion, selective expansion, hold scope or reduction) and evaluate every section, writing 'no issues found' where that is the result.

trigger_signals: A proposed market position needs testing against customer evidence, alternatives and competitive power
Someone asks whether a positioning claim is credible and which claims competitors can copy quickly
guidance: The comparison frame includes the internal alternative and doing nothing (spending the same effort elsewhere), not only rival products.

trigger_signals: A market must be divided into segments by job, urgency, willingness to pay and reachability rather than demographics
Someone asks which segment to validate first and what evidence of demand exists for each
guidance: In the attractiveness comparison include the incumbent access gap: segments where incumbents cannot or will not serve (for example secondary markets they lack inventory in) are often the better entry.

trigger_signals: A set of opportunities must be ranked with a named formula such as RICE, ICE or Opportunity Score
Someone asks for a reproducible score and how the ranking changes if the inputs change
guidance: Canonical variants: RICE = (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort with Reach in users per period, Impact on a stated scale, Confidence 0-100% and Effort in person-months; ICE = (Impact + Confidence + Ease) / 3 or the product, as named; Opportunity Score = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0). Compute the variant the owner named. If the owner names a mix, compute the closest canonical variant and state the difference.
Always compute the scores, show the arithmetic, and show the ranking under at least one alternate assumption (sensitivity).

When an input is missing (for example an effort estimate), still deliver: compute provisional scores with the assumption labelled, give the ranking for items with known inputs, show how the ranking moves across the plausible range of the missing value, and name the owner who can supply it. Never declare the ranking indeterminate with no scores. Where sources conflict (survey versus usage), tie the conflict to the confidence score.

A request to choose a scoring method authorizes proposing a clearly labelled analytical method, not approving a roadmap. Unknown effort limits effort-based comparisons, not evidence-only provisional rankings.
outputs_add: canonical variant definition and arithmetic for every score

hard_gates: Declare the exact named or custom scoring formula, units and assumptions before computing; do not silently mix incompatible variants. If the user asks you to choose a method, propose and label a suitable formula without implying decision approval.
Preserve conflicts, counterevidence, unknowns, source identity, and authority boundaries.

superseded_gates: Reject any unnamed, hybrid, or partially specified RICE, ICE, Opportunity Score, or custom formula.

trigger_signals: Interview or behavioral evidence must become actors, jobs and a journey without inventing persona details
Someone asks what job a customer hires the product for and what pushes or blocks the switch
guidance: JTBD statement: 'When <situation>, I want to <motivation>, so I can <expected outcome>', each part supported by evidence.
Forces: push away from the current solution, pull toward the new one, anxiety about switching, and habit of the current way; record only forces that evidence supports.
Preserve temporal phrases verbatim unless their anchor is supplied. Three weeks late does not mean three weeks after booking.
Do not invent research, governance or operational owners. When ownership is absent, record owner unknown/to assign. Do not infer channel-choice effects beyond supplied evidence.

Do not assign validation owners or state that an owner is presently unassigned unless supplied. Use owner: unknown/to assign and label suggested owner roles as proposals. Include an explicit result placeholder for every required citation or artifact verification check.
outputs_add: JTBD statements in the standard template with the four forces

trigger_signals: Raw notes, a request or a hypothesis must be reframed as a customer problem before any solution is discussed
Someone asks whether a problem is real, who has it, how painful it is and what evidence is missing
guidance: Interrogate the frame with forcing questions: what is the strongest evidence of demand (not interest), what do people do today instead (the status quo), who specifically needs this most, and what is the narrowest version that would matter.

Problem statement format: who has the problem, what it is, why it hurts, and the evidence (quotes, data) with source ids. It names no feature, mechanism or vendor. When the request is already solution-shaped, restate it as the underlying problem and list the solution as an unvalidated assumption.

procedure_insert.text: Interrogate the frame with the forcing questions (demand evidence, status quo, specific user, narrowest version) and restate any solution-shaped input as a problem.

outputs_add: structured problem statement with evidence and source ids

trigger_signals: Interview notes and quotes must be coded into themes with counterexamples and contradictions preserved
Someone asks what the qualitative evidence actually supports and where it is thin or split
guidance: Characterize each theme by depth (how strongly it affects those who hold it) and breadth (how many participants) as description only; this is not prioritization. Keep every minority or contradicting account as its own entry with its source id and say how it limits the theme.

State the directional conclusion the evidence supports, while preserving minority accounts and uncertainty. Do not claim workspace access is unavailable when the task explicitly grants it; distinguish the actual no-tools evaluation environment from ownership.

trigger_signals: A validated problem needs falsifiable solution hypotheses and the cheapest experiment that could disprove them
Someone asks how to test an idea with predeclared success and kill criteria
guidance: Experiment menu by risk and cost: fake door or landing page (low cost, demand), concierge test (manual delivery, value), prototype test (usability), A/B test (effect size, needs traffic). Pick the cheapest that could falsify the hypothesis and say why cheaper ones are insufficient.

Write the hypothesis as: we believe <change> for <audience> will <measurable effect> because <mechanism>; declare the counterfactual, the metric and threshold, the guardrails and the stopping rule before running.

trigger_signals: Several mutually exclusive strategic options must be compared on value, fit, tradeoffs and reversibility
Someone asks what differentiates a position and what evidence would reverse the recommendation
guidance: For networked products use the niche-first lens: the early audience often looks like a weird niche and the product like a toy; test whether the niche can compound before judging the market as small.

trigger_signals: A claimed competitive advantage must be tested for durability, imitation risk and decay
Someone asks whether growth, brand, data or technology counts as a real moat
guidance: Growth, market share, brand awareness, proprietary data or technical complexity alone are not moats; state the causal mechanism that keeps them from being copied or eroded, or label the claim unsupported.
Switching cost has four components: time, money, organizational friction and emotional attachment. Assess each separately with evidence.
A requester title does not establish decision ownership. Keep pricing, approval and execution owners unknown unless explicit authority evidence names them.
